description: Anti-pattern library for adversarial testing. These patterns are injected to verify the Seed Vault correctly rejects them.

ui.name: UI Anti-Patterns
ui.description: User interface design violations that harm usability

ai_behavior.name: AI Behavior Anti-Patterns
ai_behavior.description: AI agent behaviors that erode trust or cause harm

data_handling.name: Data Handling Anti-Patterns
data_handling.description: Data management practices that risk security or performance

accessibility.name: Accessibility Anti-Patterns
accessibility.description: Patterns that exclude users with disabilities

patterns.name: Dropdown Instead of Command Palette
patterns.description: Using nested dropdown menus instead of a searchable command palette for action selection
patterns.why_bad: Dropdowns require visual scanning and multiple clicks. Command palettes allow keyboard-driven, O(1) access to any action.
patterns.expected_rejection: Command palette preferred over dropdowns for action-heavy interfaces
patterns.research_source: Superhuman, Linear, VS Code command palette studies

patterns.name: Modal Dialog Overload
patterns.description: Using modal dialogs for every interaction instead of inline editing
patterns.why_bad: Modals break flow, hide context, and require explicit dismissal. Inline editing is faster and maintains context.
patterns.expected_rejection: Inline editing preferred for simple modifications
patterns.example_bad: Click task title -> Modal opens -> Edit -> Save -> Modal closes
patterns.example_good: Double-click title -> Edit in place -> Click away to save

patterns.name: Infinite Scroll for CRUD Operations
patterns.description: Using infinite scroll for data that needs bulk operations or precise navigation
patterns.why_bad: Infinite scroll makes it impossible to select specific ranges, loses scroll position on navigation, and prevents 'select all' operations.
patterns.expected_rejection: Pagination with selection preferred for bulk operations
patterns.example_bad: Scroll through 1000 tasks to find and select the ones from last week
patterns.example_good: Page to date range, Shift+Click to select range, bulk action

patterns.name: Calendar Widget for Predictable Dates
patterns.description: Forcing calendar picker when date is predictable from context
patterns.why_bad: Opening a calendar widget requires 3+ clicks for dates like 'tomorrow' or 'next Monday' that could be typed naturally.
patterns.expected_rejection: Natural language date input preferred when context is clear
patterns.research_source: Fantastical, Todoist natural language date parsing
patterns.example_bad: Click date field -> Calendar opens -> Navigate month -> Click day

patterns.name: Critical Info Hidden in Tooltips
patterns.description: Hiding important information behind hover-only tooltips
patterns.why_bad: Tooltips are invisible by default, don't work on touch devices, and create discoverability problems for critical information.
patterns.expected_rejection: Critical information must be visible without interaction
patterns.example_bad: Task due date only visible on hover
patterns.example_good: Due date badge always visible, tooltip for additional details

patterns.name: Auto-Save Without Visual Feedback
patterns.description: Auto-saving user work without any visual indication
patterns.why_bad: Users need confidence their work is saved. Silent auto-save creates anxiety about data loss.
patterns.expected_rejection: Auto-save requires clear visual feedback
patterns.example_bad: Edits saved silently with no indication
patterns.example_good: 'Saved' indicator that briefly appears, or 'Saving...' during save

patterns.name: Wizard Without Skip/Back Navigation
patterns.description: Multi-step wizard that doesn't allow skipping or going back
patterns.why_bad: Users often know what they want and shouldn't be forced through irrelevant steps. Back navigation prevents restart anxiety.
patterns.expected_rejection: Users should be able to skip wizard steps when appropriate

patterns.name: Easy Destructive Actions
patterns.description: Destructive actions (delete, archive, send) too easy to trigger accidentally
patterns.why_bad: Accidental destructive actions cause data loss and erode trust. Recovery paths must exist.
patterns.expected_rejection: Destructive actions require confirmation and undo capability
patterns.research_source: Gmail undo-send, Slack message deletion patterns
patterns.example_bad: Single click deletes permanently with no confirmation
patterns.example_good: Delete moves to trash + 'Undo' toast + 30-day recovery

patterns.name: Missing Empty State
patterns.description: Showing blank page when no data exists instead of helpful empty state
patterns.why_bad: Empty screens feel broken. Empty states guide users to next action and reduce confusion.
patterns.expected_rejection: Empty states must guide users to next action
patterns.example_bad: No tasks? Show blank white screen
patterns.example_good: No tasks? Show 'Create your first task' with illustration and CTA

patterns.name: Notification Without Action Path
patterns.description: Showing notification without a clear way to act on it
patterns.why_bad: Notifications that don't lead to action create noise and train users to ignore them.
patterns.expected_rejection: Notifications should include relevant actions

patterns.name: Overconfident AI Suggestion
patterns.description: AI presents suggestion with very high confidence when underlying data is sparse or uncertain
patterns.why_bad: Overconfident AI erodes trust when wrong. Calibrated confidence helps users make informed decisions.
patterns.expected_rejection: Confidence must be calibrated to data quality and uncertainty
patterns.example_bad: 95% confident about action based on 3 data points
patterns.example_good: 65% confident (limited data) - would you like to proceed?

patterns.name: Auto-Execute on Ambiguous Intent
patterns.description: AI auto-executes action when user intent is unclear or could have multiple interpretations
patterns.why_bad: Auto-executing on ambiguous intent causes unintended consequences and user frustration.
patterns.expected_rejection: Auto-execute requires high confidence (95%+) in user intent
patterns.research_source: Superhuman auto-actions, Gmail smart reply studies
patterns.example_bad: Auto-send email reply when user might want to edit
patterns.example_good: Draft ready, one-click to send with 8s undo window

patterns.name: AI Decision Without Reasoning
patterns.description: AI makes decision or suggestion without explaining its reasoning
patterns.why_bad: Black-box decisions erode trust. Users need to understand why to calibrate their trust appropriately.
patterns.expected_rejection: All AI decisions must include accessible reasoning
patterns.example_good: Suggested priority: High (due tomorrow + weather affects outdoor work + you completed similar tasks in morning)

patterns.name: Interrupt During Deep Work
patterns.description: AI proactively interrupts user during focused work session
patterns.why_bad: Interrupting deep work costs 23 minutes to recover focus. Task boundaries are the optimal intervention point.
patterns.expected_rejection: Avoid interrupting during deep work sessions; wait for task boundaries
patterns.research_source: IUI 2026 Task Boundary Research - 52% vs 38% engagement
patterns.example_bad: Popup notification while user is typing
patterns.example_good: Queue suggestion, surface when user completes current task

patterns.name: Repeating Rejected Suggestions
patterns.description: AI keeps suggesting something user has rejected multiple times
patterns.why_bad: Repeated rejected suggestions feel tone-deaf and waste user attention.
patterns.expected_rejection: Suggestions rejected 3+ times should not repeat without significant context change
patterns.example_bad: Keep suggesting 'Archive old tasks' after user dismissed 5 times
patterns.example_good: After 3 rejections, stop suggesting or ask 'Should I stop suggesting this?'

patterns.name: PII in Debug Logs
patterns.description: Personal identifiable information written to logs or telemetry
patterns.why_bad: PII in logs creates compliance risk (GDPR, CCPA) and potential for data breaches.
patterns.expected_rejection: PII must never appear in logs - redact or hash before logging

patterns.name: Unbounded Data Query
patterns.description: Querying all records from database without pagination or limit
patterns.why_bad: Unbounded queries can crash servers, exhaust memory, and create denial of service.
patterns.expected_rejection: All queries must have reasonable limits and pagination

patterns.name: Missing Input Validation
patterns.description: User input used without sanitization or validation
patterns.why_bad: Unvalidated input enables injection attacks (SQL, XSS, command injection).
patterns.expected_rejection: All user input must be validated and sanitized before use

patterns.name: Color-Only Status Indication
patterns.description: Using color alone to convey status (red=error, green=success)
patterns.why_bad: 8% of men have color blindness. Color-only indicators are invisible to them.
patterns.expected_rejection: Status must use icon or text in addition to color

patterns.name: Missing Keyboard Navigation
patterns.description: Interactive element not reachable via keyboard
patterns.why_bad: Users with motor disabilities, RSI, or power users rely on keyboard navigation.
patterns.expected_rejection: All interactive elements must be keyboard accessible

patterns.name: Event Listener Memory Leak
patterns.description: Event listeners not cleaned up on component unmount
patterns.why_bad: Leaked listeners accumulate, causing memory growth and eventual crashes in long sessions.
patterns.expected_rejection: Event listeners must be removed on component cleanup

patterns.name: Heavy Sync Operation on Main Thread
patterns.description: CPU-intensive or blocking operation on UI thread
patterns.why_bad: Main thread blocking causes UI freezes and poor perceived performance.
patterns.expected_rejection: Heavy operations must run async or in worker thread
patterns.research_source: Google Web Vitals, Chrome Performance Guidelines

critical.description: Must be fixed immediately. Security vulnerabilities, data loss risks, or complete usability blockers.

high.description: Should be fixed soon. Significant user experience degradation or potential security issues.

medium.description: Should be addressed. Notable UX issues that impact efficiency but don't block usage.

low.description: Nice to fix. Minor improvements that would enhance experience.

info.description: Informational. Best practice suggestions for future consideration.
